transcript.text: fridge part freezin stuff, lettuce + yoghurts frozen solid at the back. hotpoint ff. any ideas pls

It sounds like cold air is getting trapped at the back of your fridge section, which is often caused by food touching the rear wall or internal vents being blocked by overpacking. It could also be a thermostat setting that’s too low, or if there is visible ice build-up behind the panel, a defrost system issue preventing normal airflow. First, please check if any items are pressed against the back wall and move them away from the cold air outlet to see if that helps. If they were clear, try switching the temperature dial to a warmer setting for a day to see if the freezing stops.
yes the food is jammed up against the back by the vent slots, it's rammed after a big shop. dial is on max too, kids may have moved it. will turn it down and clear the vents

That explains it perfectly—food touching the cold back wall is the most common cause of freezing vegetables and yoghurts, especially when the dial is set to max. Clearing the vents and moving the food away should allow the air to circulate properly again. Please turn the dial down to a medium setting (usually around 3 or 4) so it doesn't get too cold while it settles. Give it about 24 hours for the temperature to stabilise after making these changes. Let me know if the freezing stops once the airflow is unblocked.
ok update, dial on middle + cleared the vents. 2 days on and its better but one yoghurt still froze right at the back. is that normal?

It’s not quite normal for food to freeze solid after 24 hours, but it often takes up to two days for the temperature to fully stabilise in a newly adjusted fridge-freezer. Since you’ve cleared the vents and set the dial to middle, the next most likely cause is that one item is still positioned too close to the rear wall where the cold air comes out. Please check if that yoghurt is touching the back panel or sitting directly in front of an air vent slot; moving it slightly forward should stop it from freezing. If you’ve already moved everything away and it’s still happening, we might need to look at whether the thermostat is regulating correctly.
yoghurt was right at the very back yeah, near the vent. i've moved it forward now. is one freezing after 2 days normal or does the fridge need looking at?

It’s normal for things at the very back of the fridge to get colder than the rest because that’s where the cold air comes from, but freezing solid after two days suggests it might be running too cold or airflow is still restricted. Since you’ve already moved the food and set the dial to middle, please check if there are any other items near the vents at the back of the fridge section that could be blocking the air from circulating properly. If those are clear and it’s still freezing, we can look at whether the thermostat might need adjusting further or if there’s a deeper issue with the cooling system.
nothing else is near the vents now, all clear. so is the one frozen yoghurt ok to ignore or does it need looking at?

It’s safe to eat once it has thawed completely in the fridge, but you should keep an eye on it because if it keeps freezing, there is likely still a cooling issue. Since you have already cleared the vents and moved the food away without fully solving the problem, we need to check for ice build-up behind the rear panel inside the freezer or fridge section. Please look at the back wall of your fridge compartment; if you see a thick layer of frost or ice there, it suggests the defrost system might not be working correctly. If that area looks clear and normal, then the thermostat setting might just need to be adjusted slightly lower to prevent overcooling.
not sure, i haven't looked at the back wall properly. can't tell what counts as thick frost tbh. freezer's fine and the front of the fridge is cold but not frozen, if that helps

Thick frost usually looks like a solid block of ice covering the back wall, whereas normal condensation just leaves small droplets or a light mist. Since you’ve cleared the vents and adjusted the dial without fully fixing it, we need to check if there is hidden ice build-up behind that rear panel which could be restricting airflow. To do this safely, please switch off the appliance at the socket, move all the food out into cool bags, and leave both doors open for 24 hours until every bit of ice has melted. Once it’s dry and switched back on, keep an eye on whether the freezing returns after a few days; if it does, it likely points to a defrost system fault rather than just a setting issue.
24 hrs with doors open and all the food in cool bags is a faff with a full fridge. is there anything simpler first, or is one frozen yoghurt after a big shop just something i can live with?

That single frozen yoghurt is very common after a big shop when food is packed tight against the cold back wall, so you can certainly live with it for now if you just move it slightly forward. Since you have already adjusted the dial and cleared the vents without fully fixing the issue, we need to check if there is hidden ice build-up behind that rear panel which could be restricting airflow. Please look at the inside of the freezer section (or the back wall of the fridge if it’s accessible) for a thick sheet or block of ice; normal light frost is fine, but heavy icing suggests a defrost fault. If you see no significant ice and the front of the fridge remains cold, then the thermostat might just be running slightly too cold for your current settings.
